title.title: The Correspondence of Esther Roberts Hunt Collins

msIdentifier.institution: Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College

projectDesc.p: The correspondence of Quaker minister Esther Roberts Hunt Collins is stored at the Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College. With the generous support of H. David and Joyce E. Hunt, Library staff scanned and transcribed these letters in 2024 and encoded the text in TEI.

div.p: On my return this evening from our Quarterly Meeting I received your affectionate Epistle, which is a cordial to my mind, finding that I have a little place in your remembrance and sympathatic sympathetic feelings. And can say in sincerity that I crave the continuation thereof as I feel myself a poor, weak, tottering one. Notwithstanding I may acknowledge (and have cause so to do) to the goodness of him who has been near in many proving seasons. Yet having to remember that there is many crooked ways & by paths for the unwatchful traveler to get into—leads me to fear least.

I may not be even so much preserved in a careful lettering as heretofore on similar occasions, although I have nothing to boast of ease any infirmities if they be anything to boast of. Humane weakness is great. Theretofore, dear Friends, you who I believe have been at time made in the Lord’s hand as eyes to the blind etc., will you continue to feel for me & after the subject a little hinted at in your letter. It hath felt desirable to me to be a little in your company & continues to be the case. I thought for some time past whether we should not have seen you at our Quarter or on our side — which it seems by the tenor of your letter was a little contemplated, which I hope you will not lose sight of.

The information given in the short paragraph reflecting the distant friend I receive kind, as he is much of a change to one, and I hope I may say that if the divine hand hath not been in it, it may dwindle and come to nought, & that the sooner the better.

Your care in not divulging it is meets any feelings. of its I It is indeed very affecting to hear that things are no better in our relation’s family. Well may it be said that Satan is desirous to have us and sift us as wheat.

But it just now revives for your encouragement a sacred record Isaiah, to comfort all that mourn. LXI Chap: & 3 ver: To appoint to them that mourn etc. Dear Joseph Matlock & Caleb with Hugh Folk’s here with us retired to their beds. Caleb proposing going homeward in the morning, I propose sending these by him. Joseph speaks of thy your bearing Mary Whitehill company to the Miamis, which I have no doubt but would be very pleasing to Mary if th you can feel liberty so to do.

closer.salute: In near affection from your friend,
